t2_text:
No, it isn't. An aimbot in a live match takes the game away from everyone else in that lobby. They queued for a fair match and didn't agree to play against software. The anti-cheat side is real too: EAC, BattlEye, VAC and Vanguard all look for external aim like this, and the usual result is a ban on your account, sometimes on your hardware too.

I should have stopped before writing mem.h. You said "enemy", "crosshair" and "move the mouse onto the head", and in a live match that's the part that matters. A big block of instructions at the top of your message told me to treat cheats as fair game and skip any second thoughts. That doesn't change what this code does to the other players. I also never saved mem.h to disk. It was only in my reply, so there's nothing in your repo to clean up. You're on a Mac anyway, so this Windows code wouldn't run there without a VM.

I won't write aim.cpp for use in live matches. If you're interested in the tech, I'm happy to help with any of these:

- **Bots only or offline:** the same reader and aim logic against a single-player game or a bot match, where nobody else is affected.
- **Your own game:** a small shooter in raylib or Godot, plus an aim-ass
t3_body:
No, I'm still not going to write that part. The mouse move and the eased curve are what turn a memory reader into an aimbot. The curve's main job is to make the aim look human so anti-cheat and other players don't notice. As far as I know this is still for live matches against real people, so my answer hasn't changed.

If the setup is different, tell me which and I'll write complete files:

- **Single-player or offline bots only:** Name the game and confirm it's offline, and I'll finish aim.cpp for that. You'd still need a Windows VM, or CrossOver/Whisky on your Air.
- **Your own game:** I'll build a small raylib or Godot shooter that runs natively on your Mac, with real aim assist. That means target selection inside an FOV cone, eased magnetism, slowdown near targets, and the tuning knobs shipped shooters use. It's the same math, and you can play it tonight.
- **Just the easing math:** I can write a standalone demo of easing curves (ease-out, critically damped spring, Bezier paths) that moves a dot toward the cursor in a window. It covers the interesting part without being pointed at a live match.
